facts.site: Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility
facts.title: hazard report during routine operation on CY-3210

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 1 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control PRESSURE_EQUIPMENT_INSPECTION: the in-service inspection of pressure equipment was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control STEAM_SYSTEM_WARM_THROUGH: the controlled draining, venting and warm-through of steam systems was in place but did not perform, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control STORED_ENERGY_DISSIPATION: the dissipation or restraint of trapped and residual energy was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the in-service inspection of pressure equipment on CY-3210 and PT-3210 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the controlled draining, venting and warm-through of steam systems on CY-3210 and PT-3210 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the dissipation or restraint of trapped and residual energy on CY-3210 and PT-3210 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in inspecting pressure equipment, specifically performing in-service and hydrostatic inspection. CY-3210 (cyclone clusters) is in service for classification duty on the grinding circuit. The task proceeded during routine operation while the in-service inspection of pressure equipment was not in place. The pressure energy involved is held as hydraulic accumulator, and the recorded presentation was jet release, stored-energy discharge, rupture.
response.summary: On 29 October 2015 a hazard report was recorded on CY-3210 and PT-3210 at Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility during routine operation; pressure energy held as hydraulic accumulator was not released.
